subject: history
title: Building the Dictatorship Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll see Hitler turn Chancellor's office into total dictatorship in 19 months.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Reichstag Fire, Enabling Act and Night of the Long Knives.
final_note: You learned how Hitler became Führer by August 1934.

walkthroughs.body_html:
On 27 February 1933 the Reichstag burned down — Dutch communist van der Lubbe was blamed.

Hitler used emergency decrees to arrest 4,000 communists. On 23 March 1933 the Enabling Act let him make laws without parliament for four years.

Trade unions were banned in May 1933 and replaced by the German Labour Front.

On 14 July all parties except the Nazis were outlawed. State governments lost power. This process — Gleichschaltung — turned Germany into a one-party state within months.

walkthroughs.h2: Night of Long Knives and Führer
walkthroughs.body_html:
SA leader Ernst Röhm wanted a 'second revolution'. The army hated him.

On 30 June 1934 the SS killed Röhm and rivals in the Night of Long Knives. President Hindenburg died on 2 August. Hitler merged Chancellor and President into one title: Führer. The army swore personal loyalty.

mcqs.q: What was the political significance of the Reichstag Fire?
options: The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.
Hitler used it to issue the Reichstag Fire Decree suspending civil liberties, jail Communists, and create the conditions for the Enabling Act of March 1933.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
Hitler personally set the fire and blamed it on the Communists.

mcqs.q: How did Hitler come to power in 1933?
options: The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.
Hitler seized power through a violent coup or revolution.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg as part of a conservative political deal, after the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag.

mcqs.q: What caused the German hyperinflation of 1923?
options: The government printing money to pay striking workers during the French occupation of the Ruhr, on top of existing reparations and war debts.
The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.
The hyperinflation was caused by the Wall Street Crash.
Reparations alone caused the hyperinflation.
